audit.whatIsWrong: Chart rows 0, 3 and 4 disagree with the packet and with their own whys[] text.
audit.why: Packet chart is Tryndamere, Skill, Tryndamere, Swain, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Tryndamere over 999 games at 56.06%. whys[0] says 'You favour L1' against a Skill row, whys[3] says 'Swain favours 4-5' against a Skill row, whys[4] says 'You favour L6' against a Skill row. The mirror also moved its chart to the packet read.
audit.corrected: Row 0 and row 4 to Tryndamere, row 3 to Swain, as matched full/content pairs with ratings and reasons.

audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension is treated as a fixed-duration ult you wait out, with no numbers anywhere.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions' — it is 120s flat and it sustains itself only while it has champions in its 650 range to drain. That makes fighting him away from the wave, or leaving his range, the actual counterplay. Nevermove 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 at 850, Death's Hand down to 3s at rank 5, Vision of Empire 22s. Undying Rage 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: The drain-dependency and the real cooldowns written into spikes[1], breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer has Swain's W and E swapped — it writes 'Nevermove (W)' and 'Vision of Empire (E)' — and calls both of them roots. It also never says where Nevermove's root actually happens.
audit.why: Nevermove is E, Vision of Empire is W. Riot's Vision of Empire text is a demon eye that damages, slows, reveals and grants a Soul Fragment — no root at all. Riot's Nevermove text: 'It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits' — the root is on the return trip, so sidestepping the outgoing wave alone does not save you, and standing off the return path does.
audit.corrected: Slots fixed, the phantom second root removed, and the return-trip root stated as the thing to dodge.

audit.why: report[8] already carries Executioner's Calling early, which is the right answer to Ravenous Flock's healing; Mercury's Treads and Doran's Shield fit the magic poke.

edits.before: Spin up fury on the wave before contesting anything. Identify how Swain contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Spin up fury on the wave — Swain has no root yet and Death's Hand is his only tool, so the level-1 walk-up belongs to you.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Demonic Ascension's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His window: Nevermove is up on 12s and Soul Fragments have stacked, so he pins you for a full Death's Hand. Give ground and farm.

edits.before: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds — dives and coin-flip all-ins become yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Swain's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds, and Demonic Ascension only sustains him while it drains — fight him away from minions and 6 is yours.

edits.before: Swain favours 4-5 — both roots online plus passive stacks let him pin you and win extended trades.
edits.after: Swain favours 4-5 — Nevermove plus stacked Soul Fragments let him pin you and win extended trades.

edits.before: Swain's window is landing Nevermove (W) or a Vision of Empire (E) root to pin you in his Q — respect the root, and once he burns it, all-in while it's down and heal the poke off with Bloodlust.
edits.after: Swain's window is Nevermove (E): it roots on the return trip, not the throw, so sidestep the wave coming back at you. Once he burns it, all-in on its 12s and heal the poke off with Bloodlust.

edits.before: Undying Rage hard-counters Demonic Ascension (R): when he pops ult to lifedrain and heal, pop R, stay on him, and out-sustain his drain — he can't kill you and you kill him first.
edits.after: Undying Rage beats Demonic Ascension (R): the form lasts only while he keeps draining, so fight him off the wave — with no minions in range his 120s ult falls away and you kill him.

edits.before: Level 3 onward it's a root check: if Swain lands Nevermove (W) or Vision of Empire (E) he pins you for full Q damage. Bait the root, trade when it's down, and your Bloodlust heal keeps you ahead. Level 4-5 he's strongest with both roots and stacks up.
edits.after: Level 3 onward it is a root check: Nevermove (E) roots on its return trip, and if it lands he pins you for a full Death's Hand. Sidestep the wave coming back, trade on its 12s, and Bloodlust keeps you ahead. Level 4-5 he is strongest with Soul Fragments stacked.

edits.before: Bait or dodge Nevermove (W) and Vision of Empire (E) root, then all-in when they're down
edits.after: Sidestep the Nevermove (E) wave on its return trip, then all-in while its 12s is down

edits.before: Land a root (W or E) to pin you for his Q and passive stacks
edits.after: Land Nevermove (E) to pin you for a full Death's Hand

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. R survives it; out-crit him. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nevermove: 12s at rank 1, 850 range, and it roots on the return trip — sidestep the wave coming back. - Demonic Ascension is 120s and holds only while he drains, so pull him off the wave. - Undying Rage: 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Track Swain's Demonic Ascension: His drain. R survives it; out-crit him. When it is down — Crit him down.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the return trip, not on the throw — sidestep the wave as it comes back at you.

edits.before: His drain. R survives it; out-crit him. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension holds only while he drains — pull him off the wave first.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on its return, so sidestep it in both directions.

edits.before: That is Swain's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Every Soul Fragment permanently raises his health — deny the kills that feed it.

notes: Two real errors: Swain's W and E were swapped throughout the content layer, and Vision of Empire was called a root when Riot's text gives it damage, a slow, a reveal and a Soul Fragment only. Nevermove's root lands on the RETURN trip, which is the whole dodge and was stated nowhere. Whether Demonic Ascension's drain can sustain itself off Tryndamere while Undying Rage is active is not in this data — not asserted.
